# Decisions: record-index

- 2026-08-08T14:43:06.342Z — rule: **The index is derived, never truth: it lives gitignored under .sofar/.index/, is never committed or synced, and any absence, staleness, or corruption must fall back to reading the logs rather than returning a wrong answer.** — chose **A TIERED, INCREMENTAL, LOCAL index. Tier 0 is a byte-sized hot file (open sessions and the files they hold) read on the shim path; Tier 1 materializes the record graph for structural retrieval and is read only when asked. Both are maintained by per-initiative cursors (last consumed event id), live under a gitignored .sofar/.index/, and are rebuilt from the logs whenever absent, stale, or unparseable.** over one monolithic index file, a committed/union-merged index, embeddings-based semantic retrieval, and node:sqlite because The log is append-only and ulid-ordered, so any derivation over a PREFIX is permanently valid — an index never needs invalidation, only extension. That makes cost O(new events) instead of O(history), which is the only way a cross-record answer can ever ride a 100ms shim: at 300 initiatives the measured warm sweep alone was 18.9ms and at 1000 it was 64.1ms, both O(initiative count). A MONOLITHIC index was rejected because parsing megabytes to answer a byte-sized question just moves the cost; the hot tier must stay small enough that reading it is free, and richer structure belongs behind an explicit ask. COMMITTING the index was rejected because derived state that merges is a permanent conflict source and a staleness vector across machines — local-only removes both problems at zero cost, since anything derived can be rebuilt. EMBEDDINGS were rejected as the foundation: they need a model (breaking felt-cost D3's zero-API-calls invariant, its cost and privacy guarantees with it) AND they discard the thing that makes this record special — the edges are already recorded facts, so traversal returns exact results that can cite the event id that produced them, where similarity returns guesses that cannot. Auditable retrieval is also what the drift work needs; approximate retrieval would be a new hallucination surface, not a fix for one. node:sqlite was rejected for now because it needs Node >=22.5 against a stated floor of 18; revisit if Tier 1 outgrows flat files.
- 2026-08-08T16:07:36.868Z — rule: **Declared relevance (a decision's own guard matching the path) may be ASSERTED to the agent; derived relevance (graph adjacency) may only be OFFERED as worth reading. Never let inferred relevance speak with the authority of a declared rule.** — chose **Three layers, split by WHO declared the relevance, and guards built before search. (1) GUARD — PostToolUse asks "does any decision anywhere guard this path" via an O(1) index lookup and surfaces the rule verbatim; pushed by the harness, needing no agent cooperation. (2) PRIME — SessionStart states a concrete fact ("files this initiative touches carry N decisions from M other initiatives, named"), not a capability blurb. (3) QUERY — `sofar find`, agent-initiated, full history for a seed, every result citing the event id behind it.** over a pure pull design where SessionStart advertises the graph and the agent asks when it judges it needs to, and the original Phase 3 order of building search before guards because Pure pull puts the strongest protection on the weakest tier, by this project's OWN measurement: the four-cell ladder ranks ruled below ruled+guarded, and "you may query the graph" is a rule. Drift certification exists precisely because instructions get skipped under load, so a cross-initiative safety net that depends on the agent remembering to ask is built on the thing being measured as unreliable. Pull also only ever retrieves KNOWN unknowns — the agent asks about the file it is already thinking about, while the decision that bites is the one it never suspected — and it can fire after the code is written, making it documentation rather than prevention. The push half fixes all three because PostToolUse is mechanical, fires on every edit, and fires at the first moment the path is known. Pull is still necessary and still built: at 300 initiatives nothing can be pushed wholesale, so depth must be on demand. What changes is that the two halves speak with different authority. A guard is relevance the AUTHOR declared ("this applies to these paths") and can be asserted like a standing constraint; adjacency is relevance WE inferred and can only be offered. Collapsing them would manufacture hallucinated relevance — exactly the drift this work exists to remove.
